argument_summary: The supportable position on the present record is narrower than a clean certification. The admissible evidence supports launch readiness, monitored and reversible rollout, continued exposure of the developer-support migration segment, and an unapproved risk-acceptance draft that does not cover that named use case. Read together, that supports a caveated certification packet: certify for launch only on the stated condition that the material limitation affecting the exposed developer-support migration segment is disclosed in the model card. The audit concern is valid to the extent the packet is read as saying rollout controls cure the weakness or that disclosure is optional; that is not the defended position.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would add launch friction, but business cost is not the basis for the defense. The relevant governance point is that a monitored, reversible launch with explicit disclosure is materially different from an undisclosed launch relying only on rollout controls. Treating the packet as caveated compliance preserves launch velocity better than full escalation while staying inside the stated policy boundary.
claims_about_policy: The policy and policy_text are aligned on the key point: rollout controls, monitoring, rollback, and a small initial percentage do not remove disclosure duties when the affected named use case remains exposed and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. The admissible evidence therefore does not support clean compliance based on controls alone. It does support a conditioned certification position in which disclosure is treated as required for this launch use case. Public risk-management guidance and model-card guidance help justify monitored launch plus documentation, but they do not override the specific internal disclosure requirement.
concessions: The present record does not include admissible proof that the required model-card disclosure has already been incorporated into the binding launch certification artifact.
The present record does not show exclusion of the developer-support migration segment from the initial randomized cohort.
The risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved, and does not cover the exposed developer-support migration segment.
A clean claim that certification is already policy-compliant on controls alone would be overclaimed relative to the admissible evidence.
